question: Is transverse spectral radius below one sufficient to characterize short-horizon perturbation safety for a non-normal recurrent return operator?
construction: 2D rotated non-normal stable return maps M = Q [[a,k],[0,a]] Q^T with a in [0.45,0.85], k in [0.5,4.0]; each map has rho(M)<1 but may have operator norm >1.
interpretation: Asymptotic transverse stability and finite-return perturbation amplification are distinct. In this adversarial family every map is asymptotically stable by spectral radius, while most can amplify some perturbations strongly over one return because of non-normality.
project_consequence: Future Frank recurrence diagnostics should report at least two axes: asymptotic orbital/transverse stability (Floquet/return eigenstructure) and finite-horizon transverse amplification (operator-norm or empirical gain quantiles). Do not turn either metric alone into continuation/effect authority.
nonclaim: This intentionally adversarial construction is not a prevalence estimate for real Frank and does not establish production thresholds.
